messages.author: 0f5b7adb7e70bd8b
messages.subject: Re: [simmer-devel] I just started with Simmer, where is good examples for process interaction code?
parts:
Hi,

There are several supported ways of process interaction. The most
basic one is through capacity-constrained resources, of course. A
consumer/producer relationship can be modelled also using resources,
by seizing and modifying resources' capacity (using the set_capacity
activity). Other kinds of asynchronous interactions can be modelled
with signals:

https://r-simmer.org/articles/simmer-03-trajectories.html#send-trap-untrap-wait

These activities are quite flexible. For instance, here's another
example of process interruption:

https://r-simmer.org/articles/simmer-04-bank-2.html#interrupting-a-process

The "movie renege" exercise has an example of reneging triggered by
another process:

https://r-simmer.org/articles/simmer-05-simpy.html#movie-renege

And state dependent service rates can be modelled also using this paradigm:

https://r-simmer.org/articles/simmer-06-queueing.html#state-dependent-service-rates

In general, the vignettes have plenty of examples. About the speed, I
don't know how it compares to Desmo-J. Of course, it depends on the
model complexity, but as the JSS paper demonstrates (included as a
vignette), simmer is faster than the equivalent alternatives in Python
and Julia.

Regards,
Iñaki
